discovery.note: The three queries were executed against PubMed on 2026-09-12 with the documented parameters (retmode=json, retmax=100000) and the raw ESearch response bytes are committed under payloads/. Each committed payload reproduces byte-for-byte on a fresh execution of the same query, so the capture is reproducible rather than merely asserted. The slice was merged 2026-09-06 with no payloads committed and no builder, so no capture from that date survives; Q1 and Q2 reproduce the merged candidate sets exactly, and Q3 does not: the merged manifest recorded 25 candidates for that query while the query matches 58, and those 25 are exactly the set PubMed returns with retmax=25, so the merged capture was truncated rather than the index having changed. searches.pending.tsv is manifest_tool build_manifest() applied to these payloads offline. The published searches.tsv is NOT rewritten here: re-fetching changes search_id by construction, so superseding the published manifest version is a data revision and is tracked separately. See docs/audits/lct-enattah-2007-corpus.md.
